REFERRED TO COMMERCE, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND SMALL BUSINESS

items.lawCode: Amd §190, add §§192-a, 192-b & 192-c, Ec Dev L; amd §§16-d, 16-m & 16-j, UDC Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4103

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the economic development law and the New York state
urban development corporation act, in relation to establishing a
strategic network partnerships program


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :
The bill establishes a Strategic Network Partnership Program to
coordinate the delivery of services from a variety of agencies to
clusters of manufacturing industries and to other clusters of
producers of goods and services. It also creates within a Strategic
Network partnership Program a Strategic Industries Group Services
Program, to focus specialized services to industries that can make
significant contributions to the economy of New York State, and a
Supplier Network Group Services Program, to focus on small and medium
sized businesses which supply the same larger business or businesses
with products used in the manufacture and/or assembly of a final
product.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
§ 1- Amends § 190 of the Economic Development Law by adding three new
subdivisions 7, 8 and 9 to define "supplier network" and "strategic
alliances".

§ 2- Adds a new § 192-a, § 192-b and § 192-c to the Economic
Development Law.

New §192-a establishes the Strategic Network Partnerships Program
(SNPP) which is designed to organize, coordinate and integrate the
delivery of relevant services from DED, the UDC, JDA and the NY State
Office of Science, Technology and Academic Research specifically
tailored to help manufacturing industries and other producers of goods
and services. SNPP is intended to target help and stimulate self-help
activities so that such firms can improve their productivity and
competitiveness.

New §192-b establishes, under SNPP, the Strategic Industries Group
Services Program, designed to identify particular groups of industries
important to New York State that need assistance in remaining
competitive in the international marketplace and to target specialized
assistance to them, including assistance in forming strategic
self-help networks. The program is modeled on the successful
Emilia-Romagna model, in which this region of Northern Italy has
revitalized its economy through the establishment of flexible
manufacturing networks and the creation of industry-specific
manufacturing service centers.

A Strategic Industry is defined as an industry group that is
considered to be critical to the economy of the state in terms of
employment, and/or in which the state appears to have a comparative
advantage which would enable such an industry group to continue to
make a, significant contribution to the economic health of the state
or a region of the state. Subdivision 2 of § 192-b establishes an
Advisory Panel 70 designate strategic industries and a process for
reviewing such designation.

New §192-c establishes, under SNPP, the Supplier Network Group
Services Program, which is similar to the Strategic Industries
Group,services Program except that it may encompass a group of firms
in different industries that supply products to the same larger firm
or firms. Again, it encourages cooperative, self-help networks on the
Emilia-Romagna model.


§ 3-Amends the opening of paragraph (e) of subdivision 7 of 16-d of §1
of Chapter 174 of the Laws of 1968 to include associations
representing SNPP's as those eligible to apply for support under the
NYS Urban Development Corporation Act.

§ 4- Amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 1 of §16-i of §1 of
Chapter 174 of the Laws of 1968 to allow the Empire State Economic
Development Fund to provide financial, technical or other assistance
from the fund to qualified businesses and other entities, including
associations representing SNPP's.

§ 5-Amends subdivision 1 of §16-j of §1 of Chapter 174 of the Laws of
1968 by including association representing SNPP's.

§ 6- Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Manufacturing employment, and employment in related production of
goods and services, in New York State has been experiencing a
long-term decline, but manufacturing still remains a major employer in
the State, generating high-paying jobs. Many of these remaining
industries are experiencing increasingly stiff international
competition and must remain innovative and productive if they are to
survive. In addition, new, emerging industries in the State, producing
goods and services, are engaged in similar competition at home and
abroad as they seek to expand and capture a significant share of the
marketplace.  The bill is based on the premise that economic
development policy should be focused on building cooperative linkages
among groupings of firms which work together in networks or which are
concentrated in regions as sectors or clusters, linked by similar
products, shared technologies or common constraints. This idea of
cluster-based economic development considers groups of firms as a
whole and works toward developing an entire sector or cluster rather
than an individual firm.  This bill establishes a statutory framework
for the Department of Economic Development to draw upon the existing
resources of the State to help those industries that are economically
viable and can compete in the international marketplace. By using
existing modernization programs, devising new and innovative sell-help
activities, promoting, where appropriate, the formation of flexible
manufacturing networks, and by disseminating needed information, the
Department can help these industries survive by becoming more
productive and competitive. In addition, certain groups of industries,
such as the garment industry, are major employers that are currently
being threatened with major cutbacks and retrenchment. This bill
establishes a Strategic Industries Group Services Program under the
SNPP, which is designed to address the specific problems of such
endangered industry groups. The bill also recognizes as Strategic
Industries, emerging industrial groups, such as new media and
software, which have the potential to grow and expand in New York
State.  Similarly, improvements in the productivity and efficiency and
product quality among suppliers to larger firms improves the
competitiveness of both the supplier and the receiver of such
products. The Supplier Network Group Services Program is designed to
accomplish this goal.  This program is modeled on the successful
networking program established in Italy's Emilia-Romagna region which
has regenerated what was once a depressed economy. Regions in Germany
and Denmark have been successful in replicating this concept to
revitalize their economies.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-2008: A.2952; 2005-2006: A.3963; 2003-2004: A.6146-A, 2001-2002:
A.1005/S.751, 1999-2000: A.109-A/S.  550-A, 1997-1998: A.1216/S.4349,
1995-1996: A.11300.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None. The bill calls for coordinating existing programs.
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately, provided, however, that the
amendments to subdivision 1 of section 16-m of section one Chapter 174
of the laws of 1968 constituting the New York State Urban Development
Corporation Act made by section four shall not affect the expiration
of such subdivision and shall be deemed to expire therewith.
